title: Weekday deploy brief and tactical cadence — Nov 2027 (draft)
body:
Context:
This is a compact, weekday-focused deploy brief for small-batch releases targeting low-traffic windows (local weekday mornings). Purpose is to provide a concise preflight checklist, an hour-by-hour cadence for the day-of, a lightweight rollback ladder, and a first-pass draft of the release notes for comms.

Goals:
- Ship a targeted change set with minimal blast radius (API-only, non-breaking changes except noted).
- Validate latency SLOs and error-rate baselines post-rollout.
- Keep customer-facing impact to zero; if customer-visible risk detected, execute fallback.

Scope of this release:
- Service: routing-proxy (hosted-inference edge)
- Change set: traffic routing tweaks + quantization variant feature flag flip (alpha -> beta for internal tier)
- Why now: performance fix for tail latency in 2-token responses (related to kernel selection heuristics).
- Risk level: medium (kernel selection touches hot paths, but controlled by feature flag and canary).

Preflight checklist (to complete before 08:30 local deploy day):
- [ ] Merge clearance: PR green, +2 reviews, CI passed (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Smoke test matrix executed on staging: route sanity, kv-cache warmup, short/long prompt flows (owner: Joan).
- [ ] Canary images built and pushed to registry; digest recorded in ticket (owner: CI bot, verified by Priya).
- [ ] Capacity reservation: Dedicated pool has 20% overcommit for 2h (owner: infra-oncall).
- [ ] Alerts and dashboards: telemetry panel pinned, rollback runbook available in Slack channel #release-weekday (owner: Samira).
- [ ] Notify stakeholders: product, SRE, CS, and ~10 affected FE engineers (owner: Samira).
- [ ] Backup artifact: snapshot of routing config and traffic-lists exported (owner: infra).
- [ ] Communication template prepared (status page, internal comms, customer opt-in opt-out notes) (owner: Priya).

Go / No-Go criteria (must be satisfied at 09:00):
- No critical P0 alerts in last 60 minutes for routing-proxy in staging.
- Canary latency p50/p95 within 5% of baseline; no increase in 5xx or timeouts.
- End-to-end smoke generation shows successful completions for 95% of test prompts.
- If any criterion fails -> hold and triage; recommended action is to revert feature flag in staging and re-run tests.

Day-of cadence (hourly lanes) — timeline for a weekday microwindow (09:00 — 15:00 local):
09:00 - 09:30 | Preflight sync and final signoff
- Quick STANDUP: confirm owners listed above are online, Slack patch channel open.
- Final CI digest check; snapshot recorded.
- Status update posted to #release-weekday (Samira).

09:30 - 10:15 | Canary ingress (1% traffic)
- Flip feature flag for canary pool only.
- Monitor latency panels and error rate at 0/1/5 minute increments.
- Owners: Joan (observability), Ethan (deploy), infra-oncall (capacity).
- Acceptance: no error spike, p95 < baseline + 10% after 10m.

10:15 - 11:00 | Incremental ramp: 5% -> 15%
- If stable for 20 minutes at 5%, proceed to 15%.
- Check KV cache hit-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and token-per-request costs.
- Log any unusual tail latency > 250ms.

11:00 - 12:00 | Broader ramp: 30% -> 50% (internal tier)
- Expand to internal tier traffic; keep customer-tier pinned at 0%.
- Run synthetic traffic generator scenario A (short-chats) and B (long context).

12:00 - 13:00 | Lunch hold and quick audit
- Pause ramps, re-validate dashboards.
- Decision point: proceed to customer-tier or hold for afternoon window.

13:00 - 14:00 | Customer-tier rollout (if green) 75% -> 100%
- Enable routing change for customer-tier in 2 steps (75% then 100%).
- Monitor for quota-exhaustion events and errors from external integrations.

14:00 - 15:00 | Stabilization and verification
- Run post-deploy automated canary checks (end-to-end gen, embedding queries).
- Compile brief for release notes and comms; assign owners for post-release followups.

Rollback ladder (fastest to slowest):
- Immediate: flip feature flag back to previous state (owner: Ethan) -> expected <1 minute.
- Container rollback: redeploy previous image tag to canary pool -> expected 3-8 minutes.
- Traffic re-routing: shift customer traffic to fallback region (owner: infra) -> expected 5-15 minutes.
- Full rollback (if sustained P0): run orchestration play to revert to previous config and schedule hotpatch window (coordinate with SRE).

Post-deploy notes capture (template):
- Time of each ramp and check results.
- Any deviations from expected telemetry.
- Incident notes (if any), mitigation steps, and postmortem owners.
- Ticket links for bugs introduced by the deploy.

Monitoring queries / quickchecks (copied for convenience):
- routing-proxy:rate(5m)[errors] > 0.05 -> alert (sample)
- p95_latency = hist_percentile(95, routing_request_duration_ms{service=\"routing-proxy\"})
- kv_cache_hit_rate = sum(kv_cache_hits)/sum(kv_cache_lookups) over 10m
- synthetic-success = count(successful_synth_runs{scenario=\"short-chat\"}) / count(total_synth_runs)

Release notes (draft — internal first, public after 24h stability):
Title: routing-proxy: smarter kernel routing and quant variant toggle (Nov 2027)
Summary: Small patch that improves tail latency for very short completions and enables beta quantization path for internal traffic. No breaking API changes.
Highlights:
- Smarter kernel selection reduces p95 for 1-2 token responses by ~18% in internal perf tests.
- Introduced beta toggle for quant-variant-v2 (internal-only) to test memory/throughput tradeoffs.
- Fixed: routing config race that could cause 502s during rolling upgrades (edge case).
Known issues / caveats:
- Under synthetic long-context loads, memory high-water may see temporary spikes; monitoring configured and auto-fallbacks enabled.
- Customers on dedicated pools running custom quant profiles will not be affected unless they opt-in.

Communication plan:
- Internal: post brief to #release-weekday + thread in #sre. Include quick summary, any mitigations, and the release notes link. (Samira)
- External: if release remains green for 24h, publish public release notes and a short bullet in the customer changelog. If any customer-visible regressions appear, escalate to CS and prepare controlled rollback. (Priya)

Open questions and TODOs:
- TODO: confirm whether Dedicated pools should have an automatic bypass for quant-variant-v2 (action: infra team).
- Q: Should we include a short A/B eval for quality drift in the public notes? Leaning no for this micro-release. (Priya)
- TODO: attach cost delta analysis for token-per-request after ramp (owner: product-analytics).

Notes to self / informal observability hints:
- Keep an eye on the CPU->GPU spillover metric; a small uptick often precedes a tail-latency increase.
- If we see ephemeral 429 spikes at 15% ramp, check internal rate-limiter per-route settings first (fast fix).
- If any unexplained 502s appear during canary, check new kernel's memory allocation trace (likely GC-like burst).

Post-release checklist (to close release):
- [ ] Confirm 24h green window (owner: Joan)
- [ ] Publish public release notes (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Merge any small follow-up hotfixes and tag release (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Update runbook with any new rollback steps discovered (owner: Samira)

Appendix: quick links
- Canary dashboard: https://observability.redwood/dashboards/canary-routing-proxy
- Rollback playbook: https://go.redwood/runbooks/rollback-core
- Staging smoke script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/test-runner/blob/main/smoke/staging-routing.yml

End of brief.

-- Samira (draft)

Revision history:
- 2027-11-03 created initial sketch
- 2027-11-06 added hourly cadence and rollback ladder after triage run
- 2027-11-10 updated release notes draft and communication plan per feedback
